key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O₂/C₂H₂ ratio densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, reducing porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak hardness at an intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: Tuning flame chemistry is an effective control knob for optimizing wear- and corrosion-resistant coating quality on AISI 321 steel.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si coating onto AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied O₂/C₂H₂ ratio at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2; monitored process with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: Data show porosity dropped from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, adhesion rose from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa, and maximum hardness reached 1051.7 HV at O₂/C₂H₂ = 1.1.
watch_item: The best hardness and the best densification/adhesion occurred at different gas ratios, so the final setting should be chosen based on the target property balance rather than a single metric.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
